note: The upper city on its shelf just east of the falls, directly overlooking its Slums. Name and population are placeholders

args.name: Slaver Upper Camp
args.note:
[placeholder] Name from the regional overview, not approved.

Upper city of Act I's medium city: nobles and wealthier civilians. It sits on a shelf in the escarpment directly above its Slums, at the head of the only graded caravan road from the basin onto the highland plateau, which climbs the falls stream's gorge past it. Its power is that road and the last reliable water, a thin, shrinking stream that it takes upstream of the Slums; not fertile land (P28).

Food: arid farming only, on small stone terraces along the stream on the plateau (sorghum, millet, barley, teff, chickpeas; check dams, flood farming, channels off the stream), date palms along the falls, cactus and saltbush as fodder. Never enough: food is topped up by caravan, paid for in salt and sulfur cut by captives on the pan and at the acid field and carried up the escarpment road. Who buys the salt beyond the plateau is open (P28).

[provisional] Walls and a citadel are the map's drawing, not canon. What feeds the falls is provisional: springs where the plateau's groundwater meets the master fault (W2).

Population: placeholder; about 15,000 across the city with the Slums.

note: The Slums: the poor lower quarter of the same city, at the foot of the falls below the upper city. Act I's quest hub

args.name: Slums
args.note:
[placeholder] Name from the regional overview, not approved.

The poor slums of the slaver city, at the foot of the falls directly below the upper city, and Act I's safe quest hub. Their people are free citizens: slavers do not take people from the city, only escaped slaves, the wanted and fugitives. That is a practice, not a protection: nothing keeps a wanted fugitive safe here except laying low and evading the slavers. Fugitives are not branded or marked (P30).

Water: the falls stream's last cascade, with a thin line of date palms along it (P28). [provisional] Wells and cisterns as backup. Salt caravans from the pan come in along the salt track and go up the escarpment road (P28).

Population: placeholder share of the city's 15,000.
